help.intro: Weather is the safest small talk there is — at the bus stop, in the lift, at the start of every phone call. German talks about the weather with es and a verb — es regnet, es schneit, es ist sonnig / windig / kalt / heiß — and gives the temperature in Grad: zwanzig Grad, minus fünf Grad. Change is es wird + comparative: es wird wärmer, es wird kälter. The seasons are all der and take im (im Sommer). Learn the ten weather words, the four seasons and the two questions — Wie ist das Wetter? Wie viel Grad sind es? — and you have every conversation about the sky.
help.tips[0].title: es + verb / es ist + adjective
help.tips[0].text: es regnet, es schneit, es donnert, es blitzt — verbs. es ist sonnig, windig, bewölkt, neblig, kalt, warm, heiß — adjectives. Die Sonne scheint is the full-sentence version of sonnig.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Today it's raining and it's cold.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: In the south the sun is shining.
help.tips[0].check.q: Im Winter ____ es oft in den Bergen. (it snows)
help.tips[0].check.why: Weather verbs take es and the normal third-person form: es schneit, es regnet.
help.tips[1].title: Temperatures and change
help.tips[1].text: Es sind zwanzig Grad (or, just as correct, Es ist zwanzig Grad warm). Es sind minus drei Grad. Change: es wird wärmer / kälter / besser. Morgen wird es schön.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: In the afternoon it gets warmer, about twenty-five degrees.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Today it's only five degrees, but tomorrow it will get warmer.
help.tips[1].check.q: Es ____ immer kälter. (It's getting colder and colder.)
help.tips[1].check.why: A change in the weather is es wird + comparative: es wird kälter, es wird wärmer.
help.tips[2].title: The seasons and the compass
help.tips[2].text: der Frühling, der Sommer, der Herbst, der Winter — im Frühling. Weather reports split by region: im Norden, im Süden, im Osten, im Westen.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: In autumn it's often windy in the north.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: In spring it often rains in the west.
help.tips[2].check.q: ____ Sommer fahren wir an die Ostsee.
help.tips[2].check.why: All seasons are der words and take im (in dem): im Sommer, im Winter.
help.tips[3].title: The weather kit
help.tips[3].text: der Regenschirm (umbrella), die Jacke, der Schal — 'Nehmen Sie einen Regenschirm mit!' ends every rainy forecast.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: It's cold – put on a jacket and take a scarf!
help.tips[3].check.q: Es regnet stark – nimm ____ Regenschirm mit!
help.tips[3].check.why: It is der Regenschirm, and as the object of mitnehmen it is accusative: einen Regenschirm.
help.remember[0]: es regnet / es ist kalt / es wird wärmer: verb, adjective, change.
help.remember[1]: Seasons are der, months are der, and both take im.
help.context.en: How's the weather where you are? – Bad! It's been raining for three days and it's cold, only eight degrees. – Here in the south the sun is shining, it's twenty degrees. But tomorrow it gets colder, and at the weekend there's a thunderstorm coming. – Then I'd rather stay at home.
help.mistakes[0].why: regnen is a verb: es regnet.
help.mistakes[1].why: Feeling cold takes the dative: mir ist kalt. 'Ich bin kalt' describes your character.
help.hook: Rain, sun, twenty degrees and getting colder: learn to talk about the weather, the easiest small talk in German.
sentences[0].why: Weather verbs run on es: es regnet — regnen, 'to rain'.
sentences[1].why: es schneit — schneien, from der Schnee.
sentences[2].why: Noun + -ig makes the adjective: Sonne → sonnig, like English -y.
sentences[3].why: der Herbst — autumn; related to 'harvest', the season's old job.
sentences[4].why: der Sommer — summer; a near-twin of the English word.
sentences[6].english: In spring the trees turn green again.
sentences[6].why: der Frühling — spring, from früh, the early season.
sentences[7].english: In winter it is cold and dark.
sentences[7].why: der Winter — same word as English.
sentences[8].english: The sky is grey and cloudy.
sentences[8].why: Wolke + -t/-ig: bewölkt or wolkig — covered in clouds.
sentences[9].english: Today there are many clouds in the sky.
sentences[9].why: die Wolke → die Wolken — the plural of an -e noun adds -n.
sentences[10].why: Grad stays singular after numbers: dreißig Grad, like Liter and Euro.
sentences[11].english: It is raining — I need an umbrella.
sentences[11].why: der Regenschirm — rain + shield; einen shows the der-word in the accusative.
sentences[12].english: Only two degrees — it is very cold.
sentences[12].why: kalt — cold; same family, k for c.
sentences[13].english: In July it is often hot.
sentences[13].why: heiß — hot; the ß is a sharp s.
sentences[14].english: There is a thunderstorm with lightning and thunder.
sentences[14].why: das Gewitter — the storm with Blitz (lightning) and Donner (thunder).
sentences[15].english: In October it slowly gets colder.
sentences[15].why: kalt takes an umlaut in the comparative: kälter.
sentences[16].english: Today it is foggy: you can hardly see ten metres.
sentences[16].why: der Nebel + -ig = neblig — fog turned into an adjective.
sentences[17].english: In the north it is often colder than in the south.
sentences[17].why: der Süden — the south; the compass points are der-words: Norden, Süden, Osten, Westen.
